answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make each key store its own copy of the shared cedar timber registry, re-encoded with that key's address so no two copies match. At every dawn beacon, five random established auditors request 20 random blocks and need replies within 2 seconds, too fast to rebuild from one master copy. Each copy is 40 GB, so 1,000 fakes keep 40 TB on live disks while an honest agent keeps one. A missed audit sends the key to the knoll, a probation tier earning nothing for four epochs. Limit: cheap disks shrink the cost.
